title: How does error handling work with TRY/CATCH in T-SQL?
description: XACT_ABORT, transaction rollback semantics inside CATCH blocks, error functions, and rethrowing patterns for stored procedures.

data.text: **Question:** How does error handling work with TRY/CATCH in T-SQL?

T-SQL `TRY ... BEGIN CATCH ... END CATCH` works like other languages for **statement-terminating errors of severity 11+**: the batch jumps to CATCH, where error functions (`ERROR_NUMBER()`, `ERROR_MESSAGE()`, `ERROR_LINE()`, `XACT_STATE()`) describe the failure. The critical SQL-specific rules: **transactions are NOT auto-rolled-back** on every error — in CATCH you must check `XACT_STATE()` (1 = committable, -1 = doomed/uncommittable, 0 = no transaction) and ROLLBACK appropriately; `SET XACT_ABORT ON` makes most errors doom the transaction automatically (recommended for production procs); and a doomed transaction (XACT_STATE = -1) can only be rolled back — no COMMIT, even in a seemingly safe path. To propagate errors to the caller, **rethrow** with `THROW;` (or the older `RAISERROR` for custom messages).

**What TRY/CATCH catches and misses:**
- Catches: constraint violations (PK/FK/CHECK), most runtime errors, RAISERROR with severity >= 11, some compile errors are NOT caught (compile-time errors skip the whole batch; statements after a compile error never run)
- Misses: severity 10 and below (informational), some XTP/memory-optimized edge cases, connection drops (no CATCH — the client sees it)
- Errors inside the CATCH block itself propagate to the enclosing TRY (nestable)

**Transaction semantics in CATCH — the part everyone gets wrong:**
- `XACT_STATE() = 1`: transaction is active and committable — you may choose COMMIT (rare) or ROLLBACK
- `XACT_STATE() = -1`: transaction is **doomed** — a statement failed inside an XACT_ABORT or a doomed-eligible error; only ROLLBACK works; attempting COMMIT throws 3930
- `XACT_STATE() = 0`: no transaction in scope (implicit or none) — nothing to roll back
- **Nested transactions**: ROLLBACK in CATCH rolls back the **whole** outer transaction too — @@TRANCOUNT after rollback is 0, not decremented; adjust the caller's counter or structure code so callers know

**XACT_ABORT:**
- `SET XACT_ABORT ON` — any run-time error rolls back the transaction and dooms it (XACT_STATE = -1); CATCH still runs for cleanup/logging, then ROLLBACK is the only option
- The most reliable production setting: guarantees no half-committable states, no 'error but transaction still alive' ambiguity
- Note: some errors still commit-able paths (batch-abort errors) — knowing XACT_STATE covers you regardless

**Patterns:**
- **Standard proc shell**: XACT_ABORT ON, BEGIN TRAN, TRY { work; COMMIT } CATCH { IF XACT_STATE() <> 0 ROLLBACK; log; THROW; }
- **Rethrow**: `THROW;` (must be the statement, needs a semicolon before) preserves original error number/message to the caller; RAISERROR can't rethrow the original — it fabricates a new message and loses severity/number fidelity
- **Error logging**: catch → write to an ErrorLog table (with ERROR_NUMBER/MESSAGE/PROCEDURE/LINE) → rethrow so the app still sees the failure
- **Savepoints** for partial rollback: SAVE TRAN inside larger transactions — CATCH rolls to savepoint, outer transaction continues (careful with doomed states)

data.title: The production stored-procedure shell
Catch without rethrow swallows failures
data.text: If a CATCH block handles the error and returns normally, every caller — application code, job steps, upstream procs — believes the statement succeeded. Either rethrow after cleanup/logging, or return an explicit error code the caller checks. Silent catches are how data corruption travels.

Interviewers want to assess:
- TRY/CATCH basics plus the SQL-specific transaction rules (XACT_STATE values)
- XACT_ABORT ON as the production default and what 'doomed transaction' means
- THROW vs RAISERROR rethrow fidelity
- The log-and-rethrow pattern instead of swallowing errors

items: Assuming CATCH auto-rolls-back — it doesn't; check XACT_STATE
COMMITting in CATCH when the transaction is doomed (XACT_STATE = -1)
Catching, logging, and returning without rethrow — callers see success
Using RAISERROR to rethrow — loses the original number/severity; use THROW
Forgetting that ROLLBACK in a nested CATCH kills the outer transaction too
Expecting compile-time errors to hit the CATCH block — the batch fails before TRY runs

How would you design batch error logging that survives the rollback?

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: TRY/CATCH catches severity 11+; transactions do NOT auto-rollback
XACT_ABORT ON in production procs removes the ambiguity
Log with ERROR_* functions, then THROW — never swallow
data.takeaway: The CATCH block is where you clean up and tell the truth: roll back what XACT_STATE allows, log the context, and rethrow so the caller can't mistake failure for success.
